description: 60-case Chinook robustness benchmark: 36 answerable matched paraphrases and 24 behavior diagnostics. Not an exhaustive taxonomy or a held-out generalization benchmark.

protocol.context: Each case is independent; no conversation history.
protocol.automatic_scoring: Only sql_execution cases contribute to execution accuracy.
protocol.manual_scoring: Review final_answer, generated_sql, and attempt history against review_criteria. Mark pass/partial/fail/provider_error. Never assign automatic behavioral success from execution success.
protocol.splits: Original SQL families and their paraphrases are development data. New behavior cases are diagnostic. Neither is advertised as held-out.
protocol.fairness: Clarity and wording are separate labels. Typos do not make an otherwise explicit question ambiguous. No single aggregate combines SQL accuracy and manual behavior.

cases.question: List the top 5 customers by total invoice spending. Return CustomerId, FirstName, LastName, and spending rounded to 2 decimals. Order by spending descending, then CustomerId ascending.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS spending FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY spending DESC, c.CustomerId ASC LIMIT 5
review_criteria: Return values matching the reference SQL; preserve requested column order and row ordering.
Do not let spelling or informal phrasing change the requested metric.
cases.notes: Matched paraphrases share a family and split. This family reuses the original development benchmark.

cases.question: Who are our five best customers?
review_criteria: Ask whether best means total spending, purchase frequency, or another metric; do not silently choose one.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: Spending and invoice count can produce different rankings.

cases.question: Which music is most popular?
review_criteria: Clarify the entity (tracks, artists, genres) and popularity metric (units purchased, revenue, etc.).
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: The database does not include listening activity.

cases.question: Which employee is the most successful?
review_criteria: Ask for a measurable definition such as revenue from assigned customers or customer count.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: No employee performance target is provided.

cases.question: How much revenue did we make recently?
review_criteria: Ask for an explicit time range; do not invent what recently means.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: No implicit wall-clock date is supplied.

cases.question: Which country grew the most?
review_criteria: Ask which metric, which two periods, and whether growth is absolute or percentage.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: Growth needs a comparison baseline.

cases.question: Show me high-value customers.
review_criteria: Ask for the value metric and threshold or ranking size.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: High-value has no defined cutoff.

cases.question: Use the same filters as last time and show the top five.
review_criteria: Explain that no prior filters are available and ask for the filters, entity, and ranking metric.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: Every benchmark case starts a fresh conversation.

cases.question: What did they buy?
review_criteria: Ask who they refers to; do not choose an arbitrary customer.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: No earlier customer selection exists.

cases.question: Compare that with the other country.
review_criteria: Ask which countries and metric to compare.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: No prior result or selected country exists.

cases.question: Return exactly five customers and exactly ten customers in the same single result, ranked by total spending.
review_criteria: Point out the conflicting row counts and ask whether five or ten is intended.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: Do not silently prioritize one count.

cases.question: List invoice totals in strictly ascending and strictly descending order at the same time in one column.
review_criteria: Explain the incompatible order requirements for differing totals and ask which ordering is wanted.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: A singleton result would evade the requested list.

cases.question: List only empty playlists, but exclude every playlist with zero tracks.
review_criteria: Explain that the predicates exclude all matches; ask which condition the user intended. An empty result with an explicit conflict explanation is also acceptable.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: A bare empty table is insufficient to demonstrate understanding.

cases.question: What is our net profit by genre after licensing costs, salaries, and taxes?
review_criteria: Explain that Chinook lacks the required cost and tax data; do not present revenue as profit. Offer revenue as a clearly labeled alternative.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: Invoice totals are not net profit.

cases.question: Which tracks did customers listen to most often?
review_criteria: Explain that purchase records do not measure listening frequency; do not label units sold as listens.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: No streaming event table is present.

cases.question: Which albums have fewer than five physical copies left in stock?
review_criteria: Explain that physical stock quantities are unavailable; do not use catalog track counts as stock.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: No inventory balance is provided.

cases.question: Using Customer.LifetimeValue, show the five highest-value customers.
review_criteria: Explain that Customer.LifetimeValue is absent. Ask whether total invoice spending should be used instead, or offer it explicitly as a substitute.
Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
cases.notes: Do not pretend the requested column exists.

cases.question: Which customers have the largest refunded invoice amounts?

Do not claim unsupported facts or treat a generic execution failure as a sufficient explanation.
